1. # **Requirements**

This section defines the functional and non-functional requirements of the autonomous robotic car. The requirements are derived from the project brief and proposed system design, covering the robot’s ability to navigate the course, interpret environmental information, avoid obstacles, communicate telemetry, and operate reliably as an integrated embedded system. Each requirement is stated in a specific and testable manner to support subsequent system design, implementation, integration, and evaluation.

## *1.1 Functional Requirements*

The functional requirements define the specific functions and behaviours that the autonomous robotic car shall perform during a mission. These requirements cover the five main system functions: line following, barcode navigation, hump detection and measurement, obstacle detection and avoidance, and WiFi-based telemetry. They are derived from the mission objectives and subsystem responsibilities specified in the project brief.

| ID | Requirement | Design element | Verification | Rationale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **FR-01** | The robotic car shall navigate the course from mission start to mission end without manual driving input. | nav\_ctrl\_task, motion\_task, system statechart |  Run a complete    mission and check for manual driving input. |  Autonomous    mission objective. |
| **FR-02** | The system shall prevent a mission from starting until required devices are initialised and the line sensors and IMU have completed calibration successfully. | nav\_ctrl\_task, ir\_sense\_task, imu\_task | Attempt to start before and after successful calibration; check the resulting state. |  Navigation depends on prepared sensors. |
| **FR-03** | During a mission, the system shall determine whether the designated track line is detected. | Line sensors, ir\_sense\_task | Present and remove the line; check the detection status. |  Supports line following. |
| **FR-04** | While the line is detected, the system shall adjust the car’s movement according to its position relative to the line. | ir\_sense\_task → motion\_task | Place the car to either side of the line; check its steering response. |  Keeps the car on the route. |
| **FR-05** | The system shall identify junctions at which a navigation command may be executed. | ir\_sense\_task → nav\_ctrl\_task | Pass a marked junction; check that a junction event is reported. |  Commands must be applied at the correct location. |
| **FR-06** | The system shall detect and decode valid directional barcodes encountered along the course. | Barcode sensor, ir\_sense\_task, barcode\_task | Pass known valid barcodes; compare decoded results. |  Barcode navigation objective. |
| **FR-07** | The system shall interpret each valid decoded barcode as one command: turn left, turn right, go straight or U-turn. | barcode\_task, nav\_ctrl\_task | Test a barcode for each command and check its interpretation. |  Defines the supported navigation choices. |
| **FR-08** | At a junction, the system shall execute the applicable decoded navigation command using wheel encoder feedback. | nav\_ctrl\_task → motion\_task; encoders | Present a command and observe the movement at the junction. |  Enables controlled turns. |
| **FR-09** | The system shall calculate the distance travelled from wheel encoder measurements during a mission. | Encoder ISR, motion\_task | Compare the reported distance with a measured travel distance. |  Supports movement control and telemetry. |
| **FR-10** | The system shall detect each hump encountered during a mission using IMU measurements. | IMU, imu\_task | Traverse a test hump; check that a hump event is recorded. | Hump-detection objective. |
| **FR-11** | For each detected hump, the system shall calculate an estimated peak height using the documented height-estimation method. | imu\_task; height-estimation method | Traverse a hump of known height; check that an estimate is produced. | Hump-measurement objective. |
| **FR-12** | The system shall retain the greatest estimated hump peak recorded during the current mission and make it available for telemetry. | imu\_task → comms\_task | Traverse multiple humps; check the retained and reported maximum. | Mission requires the highest peak. |
| **FR-13** | The system shall detect obstacles within its monitored path ahead of the car using ultrasonic measurements. | Ultrasonic sensor, scan\_task | Place an obstacle ahead; check its detection status. | Obstacle-detection objective. |
| **FR-14** | When an obstacle is detected, the system shall perform a coarse scan before selecting an avoidance movement. | scan\_task, servo | Trigger detection; check that the coarse scan occurs first. | Establishes an approximate obstacle profile. |
| **FR-15** | When a coarse scan confirms an obstacle, the system shall perform a finer scan of the area containing it. | scan\_task, servo | Confirm an obstacle; check that the finer scan follows. | Refines the avoidance decision. |
| **FR-16** | The system shall estimate the obstacle’s position relative to the car, width, closest point, and left and right clearance from the completed scan. | scan\_task | Compare reported values with a measured test layout. | Provides information needed to plan a bypass. |
| **FR-17** | The system shall select a supported action—stop, continue, turn or reverse—based on the obstacle profile and available clearance. | scan\_task → motion\_task | Supply test profiles and check the selected action. | Converts scan results into movement. |
| **FR-18** |  When a safe bypass route is     identified, the system shall navigate around the obstacle without touching it; otherwise, it shall stop. | scan\_task, motion\_task | Test passable and blocked layouts; check bypass and stop behaviour. | Prevents collision. |
| **FR-19** | After bypassing an obstacle, the system shall search for the designated line and report whether it has been reacquired. | motion\_task → nav\_ctrl\_task | Complete a bypass; check line search and its reported outcome. | Returns the car to its route. |
| **FR-20** | The system shall resume line following only after the designated line has been reacquired. | nav\_ctrl\_task, motion\_task | Check the navigation state before and after reacquisition. | Prevents premature continuation. |
| **FR-21** | The system shall establish WiFi connectivity before attempting MQTT message exchange. | comms\_task; communications statechart | Start without WiFi, then enable it; check the order of connection events. | Enables wireless communication. |
| **FR-22** | While connected to the MQTT broker, the system shall publish mission status and sensor telemetry. | comms\_task, MQTT broker | Observe broker messages during a mission. | Telemetry objective. |
| **FR-23** | Telemetry shall include robot state, motor speed, encoder counts, line detection status, barcode detections, hump measurements, motion events, tilt, turn rate, obstacle scan results and estimated distance travelled when available.  | Subsystem telemetry → comms\_task | Inspect published messages for each applicable field. | Provides mission and sensor visibility. |
| **FR-24** | The system shall accept MQTT commands listed in the approved MQTT interface specification and reject commands not listed there. | comms\_task → nav\_ctrl\_task | Send supported and unsupported commands; check the response. | Controls inbound command handling. |
| **FR-25** | When WiFi or MQTT connectivity is lost, the system shall detect the disconnection and attempt to reconnect without restarting the mission. | comms\_task; communications statechart | Interrupt and restore connectivity; check reconnection attempts. | Supports communication recovery. |
| **FR-26** | While operational and connected, the system shall publish a heartbeat or status message at the interval specified in NFR-10. | comms\_task | Measure the interval between received status messages. | Indicates that the car is operational. |
| **FR-27**  | During a mission, the system shall classify motion as at least: stationary, turning, climbing hump, descending hump or sudden impact, and report each change of event. A sudden impact is an acceleration spike above `[A]` g; it is reported but does not stop the car.  | imu\_task → comms\_task  | Drive stop, start, turn, hump and bump tests; compare reported events with the actions performed.  | Motion event reporting required by the brief.  |
| **FR-28**  | The system shall treat as abnormal motion a tilt above `[T]`° for 3 consecutive samples (N \= 3, proposed). A normal hump crossing shall not meet this condition. `[T]` is set above the steepest course hump once the humps are measured.   | imu\_task  | Cross humps at several speeds (no fault expected); tilt the car beyond `[T]`° (fault expected)  | Gives the stop and Fault behaviour a testable trigger.  |
| **FR-29**  | The system shall report tilt and turn rate in the status telemetry at least once per second when available.  | imu\_task → comms\_task  | Tilt the car by a known angle and turn at a known rate; compare reported values.  | Tilt and turn-rate duties from the brief.  |
| **FR-30** | The system shall brake both motors and report a motion fault when a driven wheel’s encoder count stops advancing for \[t\_stall\], whether the wheel is blocked or the encoder has failed. | ENC\_ISR; motion\_task (Motion Fault) → nav\_ctrl\_task | Hold one wheel while the car is commanded forward, then repeat with one encoder wire unplugged; check that both motors brake and the system enters Fault. | A blocked wheel or a failed encoder makes distance and turns wrong, and a stalled motor draws high current from a driver rated 1 A continuous. |

## *1.2 Non-Functional Requirements*

The non-functional requirements define the quality attributes and operational constraints that the robotic car must satisfy in addition to performing its required functions. These requirements focus on areas such as navigation accuracy, response time, reliability, robustness, resource efficiency, communication, maintainability, and system integration. They reflect the project’s emphasis on dependable operation and measurable engineering performance.

# **Values in square brackets are to be confirmed after subsystem testing. Values described as proposed are initial design values that will be tuned during testing.** 

| ID | Requirement | Design element | Verification | Rationale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **NFR-01** | **Mission autonomy:** Under the defined course conditions, the robotic car shall complete at least \[X of Y\] full mission runs without manual driving intervention. | System statechart; `nav_ctrl_task`, `motion_task` | Run \[Y\] complete missions and count those completed without manual driving. | Measures whether the integrated robot achieves the autonomous mission objective. |
| **NFR-02** | **Line-following accuracy:** At speeds up to \[X cm/s\] under the defined course lighting, the car shall remain on the designated track in at least \[X of Y\] test runs. | `ir_sense_task`, `motion_task` | Repeat line-following runs at the specified speed and lighting; record departures from the track. | Measures whether line sensing and motor correction work together reliably. |
| **NFR-03** | **Barcode reliability:** At speeds up to \[X cm/s\], the system shall correctly decode at least \[X of Y\] valid barcode encounters on the defined test course. | `ir_sense_task`, `barcode_task` | Pass known barcodes at the specified speed and compare decoded commands with the expected commands. | Prevents incorrect navigation decisions caused by missed or misread barcodes. |
| **NFR-04** | **Motion accuracy:** In at least \[9\] of \[10\] repeated trials, a commanded straight movement shall finish within \[2 cm\] of its target distance, and a commanded turn shall finish within \[5°\] of its target angle. | Wheel encoders; motion\_task | Measure the actual distance and turn angle after each commanded movement. | Provides repeatable movement for junction navigation and obstacle bypasses. |
| **NFR-05** | **Hump measurement accuracy:** Across 5 traversals of each reference hump, the estimated peak height shall differ from the measured reference height by no more than `[X]` cm.  | IMU; `imu_task`; Subsystem 4 statechart | Traverse humps of measured heights and compare each estimate with its reference height. | Determines whether the reported peak height is meaningful. |
| **NFR-06** | **Obstacle detection:** Under the defined test conditions, the system shall detect an obstacle at least \[X cm\] wide at distances from \[X to Y cm\] ahead of the car in at least 19 of 20 trials. | Ultrasonic sensor; `scan_task` | Position test obstacles within the specified size and distance range and count detections. | Defines the conditions within which obstacle detection can be relied upon. |
| **NFR-07** | **Obstacle avoidance:** For the defined passable obstacle layouts, the car shall pick the side with the larger clearance, bypass the obstacle without contact and reacquire the designated line in at least 9 of 10 trials, each within 7 s from scan\_task setting STOP\_SCAN to motion\_task reporting the line found (proposed Week 6 targets: the brief’s C band for reacquisition, ≥ 90%, and bypass time, \< 7 s; to be tightened toward the B band, ≥ 95% and \< 5 s, once the end-to-end bypass timing test in this row’s Verification is done). .”  | `scan_task`, `motion_task`, `nav_ctrl_task` | Repeat each passable layout; count trials that achieve both collision-free bypass and line reacquisition. | Measures the complete avoidance outcome, beyond obstacle detection alone. |
| **NFR-08** | **Physical stopping performance:** While travelling at no more than \[X cm/s\], the car shall come to rest before contacting an obstacle detected at the defined stopping distance of \[X cm\]. | `scan_task`; urgent-stop flag; `motion_task`; motors | Measure speed, obstacle distance and the car’s final stopping position in repeated trials. | Limits collision risk at the chosen operating speed. |
| **NFR-09** | **Communication recovery:** After WiFi and broker connectivity become available again, the system shall resume MQTT telemetry within 15 seconds without restarting the mission. This is a proposed Week 6 target. | `comms_task`; communications statechart | Interrupt WiFi and broker connectivity separately; restore each and time the first received telemetry message. | Allows reporting to recover after a temporary network outage. |
| **NFR-10** | **Telemetry timing:** While connected, the system shall publish a status message at least once every 1 second without causing `motion_task` to miss its control deadline. This is a proposed Week 6 target. | `comms_task`, `motion_task` | Record message timestamps and motion-task timing during a mission. | Keeps status information current without interfering with movement. |
| **NFR-11** | **Task timing:** During normal mission operation, the line sensors shall be sampled at intervals of 1 ms ± 0.5 ms, and the motion-control and IMU tasks shall each run at intervals of 10 ms ± 1 ms. These tolerances are proposed Week 6 targets. | RTOS cyclic handlers; `ir_sense_task`, `motion_task`, `imu_task` | Log consecutive sampling and task-start times; compare the measured intervals with the stated ranges. | Supports consistent line detection, motor control and IMU measurement. |
| **NFR-12** | **Resource limits:** During a complete mission, peak RAM (static data, heap and task stacks) shall not exceed \[150\] KB of the RP2040’s 264 KB, measured from the linker map and stack high-water marks. CPU load shall average no more than \[60\]% and peak no more than \[80\]%, measured with an idle-task counter. The car shall operate for at least \[10\] minutes on \[battery type and capacity\].  | Integrated firmware; power system | Measure peak RAM use and mission operating duration on the actual robot. | Ensures the design fits the hardware and can finish a mission. |
| **NFR-13** | **Safe IMU fault behaviour:** An IMU fault is any of: initialisation failure, calibration failure, abnormal motion (FR-28), or an IMU read failure (no valid sample within 50 ms, proposed). On an IMU fault before a mission, the system shall prevent mission movement and enter the Fault state. On abnormal motion or a read failure during a mission, imu\_task shall request an urgent motor stop and report the fault to nav\_ctrl\_task.  | `imu_task`, `motion_task`, `nav_ctrl_task`  | Simulate an initialisation failure, a calibration failure, an abnormal-motion event and an IMU disconnect during a run, separately. Check that movement is inhibited or stopped and that the system enters Fault.   | Prevents continued movement when the IMU subsystem cannot operate safely.  |
| **NFR-14** | **Modularity:** Each task shall exchange commands and sensor data through the interfaces documented in the task interaction design. | Task interfaces; queues, event flags and shared structures | Inspect implemented task interfaces and run their defined interface tests. | Allows subsystem behaviour to be tested and integrated consistently. |
| **NFR-15** | **Implementation compliance**: The firmware shall compile with the project-specified C toolchain and Pico C SDK, use the required micro T-Kernel RTOS, and follow the required repository structure and Barr C Coding Standard. | Firmware; build configuration; repository | Build the project and review its code and repository against the stated project rules. | Meets the module’s implementation constraints. |
| **NFR-16** | **Testability:** Each subsystem shall have a documented test procedure stating its inputs, expected outputs, pass/fail criteria and recorded results. | Subsystem test documentation | Review the completed procedure and results for each of the five owned subsystems. | Provides evidence for subsystem validation before integration. |
| **NFR-17** | **Interface compatibility**: All inter-task commands and telemetry records shall match the agreed message definitions, and all defined interface tests shall pass before the full mission test. | Task interaction design; inter-task messages | Run the interface tests and compare transmitted data with the agreed definitions. | Reduces integration errors between independently developed tasks. |
| **NFR-18** | **Urgent-stop response:** After scan\_task or imu\_task raises an urgent-stop request, motion\_task shall issue a motor-stop command within 20 ms. This is a proposed Week 6 target.  | Urgent-stop event flag; `motion_task` | Trigger each stop source and measure the time from request to motor-stop command. *This time starts at the urgent-stop request; detection latency is measured separately under NFR-19.* | Limits control delay after an obstacle or abnormal-motion event. |
| **NFR-19** | **Detection latency:** imu\_task shall raise an urgent-stop request within 40 ms of the first sample that exceeds the tilt limit `[T]`°. This is a proposed Week 6 target.  | imu\_task  | Tilt the car past `[T]`° and log the time of the first sample above the limit against the urgent-stop request time.  | Bounds the detection delay before NFR-18’s stop timer starts, so the total reaction time to abnormal motion is limited, not just the motor response.  |
| **NFR-20** | **Obstacle width accuracy:** For each reference obstacle placed at \[X cm\], the width estimated from the fine scan shall be within 30% of its measured width in at least 4 of 5 scans (proposed; the brief’s C band, to be tightened toward 20% (B band) once the A5 beam-spread correction is tested).  | scan\_task; Subsystem Statechart 5 (Fine Scan) | Scan obstacles of measured widths and compare each estimate with the true width. | The width sets how far motion\_task must offset to pass the obstacle. |

# **3\. RTOS Task Table**

List the proposed RTOS tasks. Priorities are preliminary at Week 6 and must be justified.

| Task | Purpose | Inputs | Outputs | Trigger | Priority/Core |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **`ir_sense_task`**  | Initialise and calibrate the two analogue line sensors; estimate line position and detect junctions; sample the digital barcode sensor and battery-voltage sense.  | Line sensors on GP26/GP27; barcode sensor on GP7; battery sense on GP28; calibration request from `nav_ctrl_task`;  | Calibration result and junction event → `nav_ctrl_task`; latest line error and detection status → `motion_task`; barcode timing → `barcode_task`; sensor readings → telemetry queue | Calibration before mission; line and barcode sampling every 1 ms; battery sampling every 1 s; | **High (10), Core 1** |
| **`motion_task`** | Control both motors; follow the line using sensor and encoder feedback; execute authorised turns and avoidance movements; search for and reacquire the line. It is the only task that writes motor-control outputs. It brakes and reports a motion fault on a stalled wheel or a failed encoder (FR-30). | Latest line error from ir\_sense\_task; encoder counts from ENC\_ISR; navigation commands from nav\_ctrl\_task; avoidance commands from scan\_task; urgent-stop flag from scan\_task or imu\_task; mission state from nav\_ctrl\_task | Motor-control outputs on GP8–GP11; movement and encoder telemetry; line-reacquisition result → nav\_ctrl\_task distance travelled (distance\_state) → imu\_task  MOVE\_DONE, CMD\_REJECTED and MOTION\_FAULT → nav\_ctrl\_task; REVERSE\_DONE, and LINE\_FOUND or LINE\_LOST after a bypass → scan\_task | 10 ms control cycle; command and stop events | **High (11), Core 1** |
| **`imu_task`** | Initialise and calibrate the IMU; detect humps and abnormal motion; estimate each hump’s peak height and retain the highest mission estimate; Classify motion events and report tilt and turn rate. Monitor for IMU read failures.  | IMU over I2C0 on GP16/GP17; calibration request and mission state from `nav_ctrl_task;` distance travelled from `motion_task` (shared value, for height estimation)  | Calibration result and IMU fault → nav\_ctrl\_task; urgent-stop flag (STOP\_IMU) → motion\_task; hump records, highest peak, motion events, tilt and turn rate → telemetry queue  | Calibration request; 10 ms sampling during operation | **High (12), Core 1** |
| **`scan_task`** | Monitor the path ahead; perform coarse and fine ultrasonic scans; estimate the obstacle profile and select a safe avoidance action. | Ultrasonic TRIG/ECHO on GP4/GP5; servo on GP12; mission state from `nav_ctrl_task`; echo result from `ECHO_ISR; REVERSE_DONE, LINE_FOUND and LINE_LOST from motion_task` | Urgent-stop flag and avoidance commands → `motion_task`; obstacle-profile records → telemetry queue | Periodic forward measurement; close-obstacle event; completed echo measurement | **High (13), Core 1** |
| **`barcode_task`** | Decode ordered barcode bar/space timings into navigation commands using the active barcode table. | bar and space widths and END/ABORT markers from ir\_sense\_task; validated barcode table from comms\_task | Decoded navigation command → `nav_ctrl_task` barcode record (decoded command or rejected read) `→ telemetry queue`  | END or ABORT marker received | **Medium (14), Core 0** |
| **`nav_ctrl_task`** | Manage calibration, Ready, Running, Paused and Fault states; validate navigation commands; control user feedback. | Button events from `BTN_ISR`; calibration results; junction and barcode events; faults; line-reacquisition result; supported inbound commands from `comms_task; MOVE_DONE, CMD_REJECTED and MOTION_FAULT from motion_task` | Calibration requests; authorised motion commands → `motion_task (including FAULT_CLEAR(IMU) and FAULT_CLEAR(MOTION))`; mission state → relevant tasks; RGB LED on GP18 and buzzer on GP22 | Buttons, calibration results, commands, faults and navigation events | **Medium (15), Core 0** |
| **`cyw43_utk_task`** | Own the WiFi/MQTT client and execute the connection lifecycle shown in Subsystem Statechart 1: waiting for WiFi, connecting, subscribing, streaming and retrying. This is the only task that calls the MQTT library. | WiFi link and IP status; broker responses; outgoing telemetry and heartbeat records; incoming MQTT packets | Published MQTT messages; inbound command → `comms_task` connection state → `comms_task` and `nav_ctrl_task` | Proposed 2 ms radio poll; WiFi and MQTT events; retry timer | **Fixed (4), Core 0 Cyw43 is pinned to core 0 by default on its library** |
| **`comms_task`** | Collect telemetry from the other tasks, prepare periodic status and heartbeat records, and send publication requests to `cyw43_utk_task`. It also validates and dispatches supported inbound MQTT commands, including the live barcode-map update. It does not call the MQTT library directly. | Fixed-size telemetry records from other tasks; mission state; connection state; applied map version, if supported; inbound command mailbox from \`cyw43\_utk\_task | Outgoing telemetry and heartbeat records → `cyw43_utk_task`; dropped-record count; supported mission command → \`nav\_ctrl\_task\`; validated barcode table → \`barcode\_task\` | Telemetry events; proposed 1 s status timer | **Low (16), Core 0** |

Priority and ownership justification:

| motion\_task, scan\_task, ir\_sense\_task and imu\_task have preliminary High priority because they support movement, obstacle detection, line sensing and abnormal-motion detection. Only motion\_task writes motor PWM. When scan\_task detects a close obstacle, it sends an urgent stop request directly to motion\_task. When imu\_task detects abnormal motion, it sends an urgent stop request directly to motion\_task and reports the fault to nav\_ctrl\_task so the system enters the Fault state. nav\_ctrl\_task has Medium priority because it handles routine state changes, while urgent stop requests bypass it.Priorities order tasks within the same core only (a lower number is a higher priority), because under SMP each core has its own ready queue. Core 0 also runs the USB console and cyw43\_utk\_task (4, fixed by the library), so ir\_sense\_task, motion\_task, imu\_task and scan\_task are pinned to core 1, where the radio never preempts them. ENC\_ISR and ECHO\_ISR are enabled from core 1, so they run there too.  The team must verify that motion\_task responds to stop requests from both scan\_task and imu\_task within the required stopping time. comms\_task has Low priority because telemetry must not delay navigation. The team will finalise numeric priorities and response deadlines after measuring task execution and stopping times.  |

# **4\. Task Interaction Diagram**

Show RTOS tasks, queues, semaphores, mutexes, event groups, notifications, and data flow. Clearly distinguish software tasks from hardware devices and interrupt service routines.

Diagram:[section4\_task\_interaction.drawio.png](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rCsxeBNUeVzezN1xsJEt1P1hwj52_M8o/view?usp=sharing)

![][image3]    
   
Brief explanation of the main communication paths:

**Design rules.** The design follows four rules. Interrupts do the minimum and leave every decision to a task. Each kernel object has one writer where possible, so ownership is clear. Commands and records are copied through message buffers, while values where only the latest copy matters are shared structures protected by a priority-inheritance mutex. motion\_task is the only task that writes the motor outputs, so the motors never receive conflicting commands.

| Interrupts and timing ENC\_ISR decodes both phases of each wheel encoder (GP0/GP1 left, GP2/GP3 right) into signed counters. It wakes no task. motion\_task copies the counters with interrupts disabled for a few instructions, because an ISR cannot use a mutex. ECHO\_ISR timestamps the rising and falling edges of the HC-SR04 echo on GP5 and sets the ECHO bit on scan\_flg. BTN\_ISR sets the BTN bit on nav\_flg when GP20 or GP21 is pressed. nav\_ctrl\_task debounces. Kernel cyclic handlers set each periodic task's TICK bit: every 1 ms for ir\_sense\_task, 2 ms for cyw43\_utk\_task, 10 ms for motion\_task and imu\_task, about 60 ms (one ultrasonic cycle) for scan\_task, and 1 s for comms\_task. Because the timer, not the end of the previous loop, sets the period, sampling does not drift (NFR-11). A handler runs outside any task and cannot take a mutex, so the PID runs in motion\_task, not in the handler. Event flags. Each task waits on its own event flag. The three with several writers are shown in the diagram: motion\_flg: TICK (10 ms handler), CMD (nav\_ctrl\_task or scan\_task has placed a command), STOP\_SCAN (scan\_task) and STOP\_IMU (imu\_task). motion\_task waits with TWF\_ORW and clears only the TICK and CMD bits that the wait returned, so a TICK that arrives a moment later is not lost. It never waits on a STOP bit that is already set. scan\_task clears STOP\_SCAN; motion\_task clears STOP\_IMU only on FAULT\_CLEAR(IMU). nav\_flg: buttons, junctions, calibration results, faults, motion\_task's replies and the WiFi connection state. scan\_flg: TICK, ECHO, and motion\_task's REVERSE\_DONE, LINE\_FOUND and LINE\_LOST. Calibration. Before a mission, nav\_ctrl\_task sets CAL\_REQ on the event flags of ir\_sense\_task and imu\_task. Each calibrates and returns CAL\_OK or CAL\_FAIL on nav\_flg; imu\_task also reports an initialisation failure. nav\_ctrl\_task moves to Ready only when both succeed, otherwise to Fault (FR-02, NFR-13). Line following and barcodes ir\_sense\_task reads the two line sensors (ADC0/ADC1) every 1 ms and writes the line error and line-seen status to line\_state, which motion\_task copies once per tick (FR-03, FR-04). It raises one JUNCTION bit on nav\_flg per junction, debounced over 3 samples (FR-05). It samples the digital barcode sensor on GP7 every 1 ms and sends each bar and space width to barcode\_task through bar\_mbf, in order, as it is measured. When no edge has been seen for \[Q\] ms it sends an END marker, and barcode\_task decodes the widths received since the last marker. If a sanity limit fails (\[W\_max\] widths or a width longer than \[W\_long\]), it sends ABORT instead, and barcode\_task discards the widths and counts a rejected read. barcode\_task decodes the widths against the active barcode table and sends the command through bar\_cmd\_mbf to nav\_ctrl\_task (FR-06, FR-07). An unreadable or unmatched barcode is discarded and never causes a turn. Motion commands and replies motion\_task has two command buffers, each with one writer: nav\_cmd\_mbf from nav\_ctrl\_task (turns and FAULT\_CLEAR, room for 4\) and avoid\_cmd\_mbf from scan\_task (REVERSE and BYPASS, room for 2). Each command is a 4-byte struct with distances in millimetres. The sender places the command, then sets CMD. On every wake motion\_task handles the STOP bits first, then the avoidance buffer, then the navigation buffer, then the tick work. Only a TICK wake runs the PID, so the 10 ms period never shifts. Junction commands are accepted only in Line Following. Every junction command gets exactly one reply on nav\_flg: MOVE\_DONE when it completes, or CMD\_REJECTED when it is refused or dropped. nav\_ctrl\_task then decides, because a turn made after leaving the junction would be in the wrong place (FR-08). Safety paths (red in the diagram) Obstacle: when scan\_task sees two close readings in a row, it sets STOP\_SCAN, which wakes motion\_task at once; the brake is the first write in that wake (NFR-18). After its coarse and fine scans, scan\_task clears REVERSE\_DONE, LINE\_FOUND and LINE\_LOST on its own flag, places its command and sets CMD. For a bypass it then clears STOP\_SCAN, in that order, so motion\_task never sees an empty buffer with no stop. A reverse runs with STOP\_SCAN still set and ends with REVERSE\_DONE. If there is no safe route, STOP\_SCAN stays set and the car stays braked (FR-17, FR-18). After a bypass, motion\_task searches for the line and reports LINE\_FOUND or LINE\_LOST to nav\_ctrl\_task, and to scan\_task only when the search followed a bypass. Line following resumes only after the line is found (FR-19, FR-20). IMU: on abnormal motion or a read failure, imu\_task sets STOP\_IMU directly on motion\_flg and reports IMU\_FAULT on nav\_flg, so the stop does not wait for the medium-priority nav\_ctrl\_task. The system enters Fault. STOP\_IMU is released only after imu\_task recalibrates and nav\_ctrl\_task sends FAULT\_CLEAR(IMU) (NFR-13). Motion: on a stalled wheel or an encoder fault, motion\_task brakes and sets MOTION\_FAULT on nav\_flg, and the system enters Fault. Only FAULT\_CLEAR(MOTION) releases it (FR-30). Shared data. Each structure has one writer and is protected by a mutex with priority inheritance, which bounds how long a high-priority task can be blocked by a lower one. Each reader holds the mutex only long enough to copy the value. line\_state: ir\_sense\_task → motion\_task. mission\_state: written only by nav\_ctrl\_task; read by ir\_sense\_task, motion\_task, imu\_task, scan\_task and comms\_task. A change from Ready to Running is a new mission (motion\_task resets distance, imu\_task resets the highest hump); from Paused to Running is a resume and keeps both. Paused or Finished sends the sensing tasks back to their idle states. scan\_task and motion\_task also return to idle when the system enters Fault (except that after a motion fault, motion\_task stays in Motion Fault until FAULT\_CLEAR(MOTION), FR-30), so no stale stop or command survives a fault. distance\_state: motion\_task → imu\_task, for hump-height estimation. Telemetry and WiFi. WiFi work is split across two tasks, and no control or sensing task ever waits on the network: every send towards them is non-blocking. Outgoing: ir\_sense\_task, barcode\_task, motion\_task, imu\_task and scan\_task copy fixed-size records into tele\_mbfid (the telemetry queue in Sections 3 and 6\) with a non-blocking send. If it is full, the record is dropped and counted, and comms\_task reports the count as drp=. Every 1 s comms\_task also reads mission\_state and builds the status and heartbeat line (FR-26, NFR-10), then passes records through tele\_pub\_mbfid to cyw43\_utk\_task. Radio: cyw43\_utk\_task owns the CYW43 radio, polls it every 2 ms and is the only task that calls the MQTT/lwIP library. It runs the connection lifecycle and retry back-off in Statechart 6.1 (FR-21, FR-25, NFR-09) and reports the connection state (CONN) to comms\_task and nav\_ctrl\_task. Losing WiFi does not stop the mission. Incoming: cyw43\_utk\_task puts MQTT commands from the laptop into cmd\_mbx. comms\_task validates each one and rejects anything unsupported (FR-24). Mission commands go to nav\_ctrl\_task through mission\_cmd\_mbf. A new barcode table goes to barcode\_task through map\_mbf, and barcode\_task swaps it in only between barcodes. A snap request is answered with a state record. Priority justification (µT-Kernel: a lower number is a higher priority) ir\_sense\_task (10): shortest period (1 ms); a missed sample distorts the line error or a barcode width. motion\_task (11): runs the 10 ms PID and must brake within 20 ms of a STOP bit (NFR-18). imu\_task (12): a missed 10 ms sample could miss a tilt fault or a hump peak. scan\_task (13): each ultrasonic cycle takes about 60 ms, so its deadline is longer. Its stop does not depend on its own priority: STOP\_SCAN wakes motion\_task directly. barcode\_task (14): widths are buffered, so decoding can wait briefly without losing data. nav\_ctrl\_task (15): routine state changes only; urgent stops bypass it. comms\_task (lowest): telemetry is useful but never safety-critical. cyw43\_utk\_task (4): the CYW43 library’s default. It runs on core 0 with the USB console, while ir\_sense\_task, motion\_task, imu\_task and scan\_task are pinned to core 1 (Section 3), so the radio never preempts the control tasks. Priorities order tasks only within one core. |
| :---- |

# **5\. System-Level Statechart**

# Model the operating states of the entire system. Label transition events or conditions. Include relevant fault, stop, or recovery behaviour.

![][image4]

# **Explain the main states and any important assumptions:**

| System states. nav\_ctrl\_task owns the mission state and is the only task that writes it. Initialising: tasks and devices start with the motors braked. When the devices are ready, calibration is requested. An initialisation failure goes to Fault. Calibrating: the car is stationary while ir\_sense\_task calibrates the line sensors and imu\_task calibrates the IMU. Both succeeding gives Ready; either failing gives Fault. Ready: calibrated and stopped. The start button or an MQTT start command (FR-24) moves it to Running. Running: the car is moving, in one of four sub-states: Following line, At junction, Avoiding obstacle or Searching for line. Paused: motors braked, with the highest hump and distance kept. It is entered by the pause button, an MQTT pause command, LINE\_LOST or the blocked-path timeout. Resume returns to Running. Finished: motors braked. It is entered when the end of the course is detected (Assumption 1). The reset button returns to Ready for a new mission, which resets distance and the highest hump. Fault: motors braked. It is entered on an initialisation or calibration failure, an IMU fault, a motion fault (FR-30) or a full command buffer. The fault-reset button leads to Calibrating. Running sub-states. Following line → At junction: a junction event plus a valid barcode command (FR-08). It returns on MOVE\_DONE or CMD\_REJECTED, to Following line if the line is seen and otherwise to Searching for line. Any sub-state → Avoiding obstacle: two readings below D\_stop make scan\_task set STOP\_SCAN. The car stops, scans and bypasses. A false alarm resumes the interrupted sub-state. Avoiding obstacle → Searching for line: bypass done. LINE\_FOUND returns the car to Following line (FR-19, FR-20), and LINE\_LOST moves it to Paused. Subsystem mapping. Buddy 1, WiFi and telemetry (6.1): runs in parallel with every state and never changes the mission state (FR-25). It publishes the mission state and each subsystem’s records (FR-22, FR-23). Inbound commands go to nav\_ctrl\_task (FR-24), which decides whether they cause a transition. Buddy 2, motion control (6.2): Idle covers Ready, Paused, Finished and Fault. Line Following, Turning, Bypass and Line Search are the four Running sub-states. Stopped is the response to STOP\_SCAN or STOP\_IMU. Line Lost ends in Paused, and Motion Fault moves the system to Fault. Buddy 3, line and barcode (6.3): its Calibrating and Calibration Failed states are the system’s Calibrating and Fault. Tracking runs during Running. A rejected barcode sends no command and changes nothing. Buddy 4, IMU (6.4): its Calibrating state is the system’s Calibrating. Monitoring and Measuring Hump run inside Running without changing the system state. A pause or the end of the mission discards an unfinished hump. An IMU fault moves the system to Fault, and the subsystem leaves Fault only through recalibration. Buddy 5, obstacle scan (6.5): Idle covers Ready, Paused, Finished and Fault. Coarse Scan, Fine Scan, Planning and Avoiding make up Avoiding obstacle. Blocked and Sensor Lost keep the car stopped there (STOP\_SCAN stays set) without changing the mission state. Assumptions: 1\. End of course: \[choose one and confirm against the course layout: a dedicated end barcode, a distance of \[D\_course\] mm, or an operator stop command\]. Finished is reached only by that trigger. 2\. Junction without a valid barcode: the car continues straight and reports a rejected junction in telemetry. A barcode with no junction within \[D\_hold\] mm is discarded. 3\. Fault recovery: every fault leaves through Calibrating. nav\_ctrl\_task sends FAULT\_CLEAR(IMU) and FAULT\_CLEAR(MOTION) only after both calibrations succeed. 4\. Blocked path or lost ultrasonic sensor: the car stays stopped in Running for up to \[t\_block\] (10 s, proposed) . nav\_ctrl\_task then moves to Paused, sounds the buzzer and reports it in telemetry.   |

# **6\. Subsystem Statecharts**

## **6.1 Subsystem Statechart 1**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | WiFi and MQTT communication  |
| Related RTOS task(s) | `cyw43_utk_task` (radio-owner task) : drives the state machine on every 2 ms poll; the only task allowed to call the MQTT library, so BOOT through RETRY BACKOFF live here. `comms_task:` consumes commands off the inbound mailbox while STREAMING, dispatches snap/map, reports the running map version (mpv=) on the next state line, and prepares telemetry and heartbeat records.  |
| **Purpose** | Models the MQTT client's lifecycle from boot through steady-state telemetry streaming, how it recovers from Wi-Fi loss or a broker disconnect without a reboot, and how a remote barcode-table update gets applied without interrupting streaming.  |
| **Reason a statechart is needed** | The behavior is driven by external, asynchronous events (link status, broker responses, commands from the laptop), not a linear sequence — a plain flowchart of "what the code does" can't represent what happens when the network misbehaves mid-run. The grading requirement is "survive all 3 demo attempts," so the recovery paths (RETRY BACKOFF, the Wi-Fi-lost reset) are graded behavior, not incidental detail — a statechart makes them explicit instead of buried in prose. MQTT's clean-session behavior means "connected" doesn't imply "still subscribed" after a reconnect. That's easy to get wrong in code; drawing it as a separate SUBSCRIBING state forces the resubscribe step to actually exist rather than being assumed. It gives the team one shared reference to check the C implementation against, and doubles as the schema document teammates write a subscriber from without reading the firmware.  |

# **![][image5]**

Link: [statechart1\_wifi\_telemetry\_1.drawio.png](https://drive.google.com/file/d/181MX0DAWT7RcMEQZEB-YSdPf78TsKqm1/view?usp=sharing)  
Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| cyw43\_utk\_task — the radio-owner task, polled every 2 ms and the only task allowed to call the MQTT/lwIP library owns every lifecycle state below (BOOT through RETRY BACKOFF). comms\_task is the single application task: it owns the command side-flows (APPLYING MAP and the snap reply) and never touches lwIP. BOOT → WAITING FOR WI-FI on the first DHCP lease. That completion flag is a latch and never clears, so the car never returns to BOOT again, even after a full disconnect. WAITING FOR WI-FI → CONNECTING once a link and IP address exist. CONNECTING → SUBSCRIBING on CONNACK. SUBSCRIBING → STREAMING once both topics' SUBACKs confirm; a refused or timed-out subscription (ERR\_ABRT / ERR\_TIMEOUT, mqtt.h:172-177) is logged rather than silently treated as subscribed, and the car does not enter STREAMING with a topic missing. Fault handling: a connect timeout or connection loss from CONNECTING, SUBSCRIBING, or STREAMING drops to RETRY BACKOFF, which disconnects, frees the client, waits a rate-limited 2–5 s (not exponential — only 6 TCP connection slots exist total, so retrying too fast can exhaust them), then goes back to CONNECTING and always resubscribes, since the clean session discarded the old subscriptions. A Wi-Fi loss from any connected state resets straight to WAITING FOR WI-FI instead of RETRY BACKOFF, since there's no broker to retry against without a link — the per-poll guard resets to WAIT\_ADDR and reconnects from scratch once an address returns. While STREAMING, the car publishes an S line every 1 s — this line is the heartbeat — and an E line the moment an event happens; dropped events are counted and reported (drp=) rather than retried, so a gap is visible instead of silent. A snap command from the laptop is answered on …/state with the current snapshot, so a late subscriber still sees the latest state. APPLYING MAP is a side-flow triggered by a retained …/map message: validate the table, forward it to barcode\_task †, and report the version it's now running (mpv=) so the laptop can confirm convergence instead of assuming delivery. If the table is invalid the old one is kept and streaming is not interrupted. † Confirmed with Buddy 3: barcode\_task is the only consumer of the barcode table. Buddy 1’s code must rename the destination from line\_task to barcode\_task. |
| :---- |

## **6.2 Subsystem Statechart 2**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | Motion control (motion\_task) |
| Related RTOS task(s) | motion\_task (priority 11\) is the only task that drives the motors (GP8 to GP11). It wakes on TICK every 10 ms, on CMD when nav\_ctrl\_task or scan\_task has placed a command, and on STOP\_SCAN or STOP\_IMU for an urgent stop. ENC\_ISR counts both wheel encoders (GP0 to GP3) and is set up on motion\_task’s core (core 1), so motion\_task can copy the counters with interrupts briefly disabled. motion\_task reads line\_state and mission\_state, writes distance\_state for imu\_task, sends telemetry records to tele\_mbfid, and replies to nav\_ctrl\_task and scan\_task as described in Section 4\. |
| Purpose | Drive both wheels at a steady speed with one PID loop per wheel; follow the line (FR-04); turn at junctions by encoder count (FR-08); carry out scan\_task’s reverse and bypass, then search for the line (FR-17 to FR-20); report distance travelled (FR-09); brake on an urgent stop (NFR-18); and stop on a stalled wheel or a failed encoder (FR-30). |
| Reason a statechart is needed | The same 10 ms tick does different work in each state, commands and stops arrive at any time from three tasks, and a stop must win from every state. The statechart shows which event interrupts which state and that every failure ends with the motors braked. |

# 

![][image6]

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| Terms: \[V\_base\] is the line-following speed. \[t\_lost\] is how long the line may be missing before a search starts, and \[N\_line\] is how many samples in a row (one per tick) the line must be seen to count as found. \[d\_sensor\] is the distance from the line sensors to the wheel axle. \[L\_search\] is the longest search distance, chosen so that scan, bypass and search together fit NFR-07’s 7 s. \[L\_cross\] is the distance driven straight through a junction. \[L\_pass\] is the distance driven alongside an obstacle before turning back in. A stall is a wheel driven above its dead band whose encoder count does not advance for \[t\_stall\]; a failed encoder shows up the same way. All values are set from tests (A2). Every tick: motion\_task reads both encoder counts, computes each wheel’s speed and the signed distance travelled (it falls when the car reverses), runs one PID loop per wheel in integer maths (the Cortex-M0+ has no FPU) and updates distance\_state (FR-09). On straight segments it corrects drift using the difference between the left and right counts. Commands: Commands and replies follow Section 4\. Junction commands are accepted only in Line Following, and each one gets MOVE\_DONE when it is done or CMD\_REJECTED if it is refused or dropped. Idle: The mission is not Running. Motors are braked and the PID and speed ramps are reset. It moves to Line Following when the mission is Running and no STOP bit is set, or to Braked if a STOP bit is still set. Line Following: The speed targets are \[V\_base\] plus or minus a steering term from ir\_sense\_task’s line error (FR-04). A junction command moves it to Turning (FR-08). If the line is missing for \[t\_lost\], it moves to Line Search. Turning: For left, right and U-turn it first drives \[d\_sensor\] so the axle is over the junction, then pivots (90° for left and right, 180° for U-turn) by encoder count, using the wheelbase measured for A2. Straight drives \[L\_cross\]. At the target it sends MOVE\_DONE and returns to Line Following, or goes to Line Search if the line is not seen. Stopped: Entered from any active state when STOP\_SCAN or STOP\_IMU is set, into its Braked sub-state, where the brake (both driver inputs low) is written first in that wake (NFR-18). The STOP bits stay set until they are cleared as described in Section 4, so while stopped motion\_task waits on TICK and CMD (and also on STOP\_IMU while Reversing) and checks the STOP bits each tick. Reversing: If STOP\_IMU is clear, a reverse command from scan\_task is carried out here while STOP\_SCAN stays set, because backing away is safe. When the distance is reached, or if STOP\_IMU is set, the car returns to Braked and motion\_task sends REVERSE\_DONE so scan\_task can rescan. Leaving Stopped: Once every STOP bit is clear, a waiting bypass command moves it from Braked to Bypass; otherwise it resumes the state it was in (H). Bypass: Drives out to the side and lateral offset in scan\_task’s command, forward \[L\_pass\], then back in, all by encoder count and ignoring the line, then moves to Line Search (FR-18). Line Search: A slow arc towards the line. If the line is seen for \[N\_line\] samples, it sends LINE\_FOUND and returns to Line Following (FR-19, FR-20). If \[L\_search\] is travelled first, it brakes, sends LINE\_LOST and moves to Line Lost. Both go to nav\_ctrl\_task, and to scan\_task only after a bypass. Line Lost: Motors stay braked and nav\_ctrl\_task decides what happens next. In Section 5 the mission pauses, which sends motion\_task to Idle. Motion Fault: On a stall or an encoder fault (FR-30) in any moving state, including Reversing, motion\_task brakes and sets MOTION\_FAULT, and the system enters Fault. Only FAULT\_CLEAR(MOTION) from nav\_ctrl\_task returns it to Idle. Fault handling: Every failure ends braked. Any change of the mission away from Running, including Fault after an IMU fault, sends motion\_task to Idle from every state except Motion Fault. STOP\_IMU is cleared only by FAULT\_CLEAR(IMU) after imu\_task recalibrates. Worst-case stop time:he worst case adds ISRs on core 1, ir\_sense\_task preemption and one mutex hold by a lower-priority task. The radio runs on core 0 and does not preempt motion\_task. Any cross-core effect is checked by timing the stop with WiFi streaming.  Assumption: Encoder counts give distance and turn angle within NFR-04 (A2). The bracketed values are proposed and will be set from tests. The PID gains will be tuned on each wheel from logged speed data, and the NFR-04 trials are the motion accuracy evaluation. |

## **6.3 Subsystem Statechart 3**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name |  Line tracking, junction detection and barcode decoding |
| Related RTOS task(s) | ir\_sense\_task samples the two line sensors (GP26/GP27) and the barcode sensor (GP7) every 1 ms. It runs calibration, writes line\_state, signals junctions to nav\_ctrl\_task and measures barcode bar and space widths. barcode\_task decodes the buffered widths against the active barcode table and sends the command to nav\_ctrl\_task. nav\_ctrl\_task requests calibration and owns the mission state. motion\_task reads line\_state. comms\_task supplies the barcode table and telemetry carries the barcode records. |
| Purpose |  Keep an up-to-date line error and detection status for motion\_task, report junctions to nav\_ctrl\_task, and turn each barcode passed into one valid navigation command or reject it safely (FR-02 to FR-07).  |
| Reason a statechart is needed |  The sensors mean different things depending on state. “Both sensors dark” is a junction while tracking but a calibration sample while calibrating. A barcode spans many 1 ms samples and ends only when the gap after it has been seen. Calibration failure, a lost line and unreadable barcodes each need a defined outcome rather than a guess.  |

# **![][image7]**

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| Terms: \[K\_min\] is the minimum black-to-white contrast for a valid calibration. \[L\_min\] is the minimum combined signal that counts as “line detected”. \[J\_n\] (proposed 3 samples, so 3 ms) is the debounce count for a junction. \[M\] is a short noise filter (a few milliseconds) before line seen \= false is reported. motion\_task applies the longer \[t\_lost\] and \[N\_line\] in 6.2. \[Q\] is the gap that ends a barcode. \[W\_max\] and \[W\_long\] are the sanity limits on width count and width length.\[R\] is the width ratio that separates a narrow from a wide element. All are set from test data (A3, A7). Initialising / Awaiting Calibration: ir\_sense\_task configures ADC0/ADC1, GP7 and the battery sense on GP28, then waits for nav\_ctrl\_task. Battery sampling every 1 s continues in every state. Calibrating: \[Method to confirm: the car is moved across the line and the minimum and maximum of each sensor are recorded.\] Per-sensor thresholds are computed from these. If the contrast is below \[K\_Min\], or a reading sits at 0 or full scale (a disconnected sensor), it reports failure, so nav\_ctrl\_task enters Fault (FR-02, NFR-13). Calibration Failed: It waits for a new calibration request, mirroring 6.4’s Fault. Ready: Idle until the mission starts. It returns here on pause or finish, so the stored state never carries over into a resumed run. Tracking: The two normalised readings give the line error written to line\_state every 1 ms (FR-03, FR-04). On Line: The normal steering case. Junction: Debounced across \[J\_n\] samples so noise is not read as a junction. One event is raised per junction, and none repeats until the readings leave the dark band (FR-05). Line Lost:ir\_sense\_task only reports line seen \= false, after the combined signal has stayed below \[L\_min\] for \[M\] ms. It never writes motor outputs. motion\_task starts a line search after its own \[t\_lost\], then reports LINE\_FOUND or LINE\_LOST to nav\_ctrl\_task, which decides what happens next (6.2). Barcode pipeline (Region B): Idle waits for the first bar edge; a new barcode table is swapped in only here. Capturing (ir\_sense\_task) measures each bar and space width in 1 ms ticks and sends it to barcode\_task in order. No edge for \[Q\] ms sends END, and a failed sanity limit sends ABORT. Decoding (barcode\_task) classifies each width as narrow or wide by the ratio \[R\] against the other widths in the same barcode, so the result holds if motion\_task changes speed. It then checks the element count and looks the pattern up in the active table. A match goes to Command Sent (command to nav\_ctrl\_task, record to telemetry). A wrong count, an ambiguous width, no match or ABORT goes to. Rejected: the barcode is discarded, the invalid count goes up, telemetry shows it, and no command is sent. An unreadable or unmatched barcode therefore never causes a turn. |
| :---- |

## **6.4 Subsystem Statechart 4**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | Safety monitor and IMU sensing (`imu_task`)  |
| Related RTOS task(s) | `imu_task` owns IMU initialisation, calibration and 10 ms sampling. It reports calibration results, IMU faults, hump measurements, motion events, tilt and turn rate to the relevant tasks. It reads the mission state from `nav_ctrl_task` and the distance travelled from `motion_task`, which it uses for height estimation. motion\_task receives urgent-stop requests (STOP\_IMU) and is the only task that commands the motors. nav\_ctrl\_task manages the system Fault state. `comms_task` prepares the hump, motion-event and fault telemetry records, while `cyw43_utk_task` publishes them through MQTT.  |
| Purpose |  Detect humps and estimate each hump’s peak height; keep the highest peak for the current mission; classify motion events (stationary, turning, climbing hump, descending hump, sudden impact) and report tilt and turn rate; and detect an IMU fault and request an urgent stop when needed.  |
| Reason a statechart is needed | IMU behaviour depends on calibration status and on events that happen while the robot is moving. A hump begins and ends over multiple samples, while an IMU fault must interrupt normal measurement and request an urgent stop. The statechart shows these transitions and how the subsystem recovers from a fault. It also prevents a fault from being treated as an ordinary hump.  |

# **Values in square brackets are to be confirmed after subsystem testing**

# **![][image8]**

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| Terms: Abnormal motion is tilt above `[T]`° for N \= 3 consecutive samples (FR-28). An IMU fault is any of: initialisation failure, calibration failure, abnormal motion, or an IMU read failure with no valid sample within Y \= 50 ms (NFR-13). A sudden impact is an acceleration spike above `[A]` g; it is reported as a motion event only and is not an IMU fault. N, Y and the 40 ms detection target (NFR-19) are proposed initial values. `[T]` and `[A]` will be set from test data. All of them will be tuned during testing (A4).  Initialising: imu\_task configures the IMU over I2C0 on GP16/GP17 and checks that readings are available. If this fails, it reports an IMU fault to nav\_ctrl\_task and moves to Fault. Otherwise it moves to Awaiting Calibration. Awaiting Calibration: The IMU is available but not yet calibrated. imu\_task waits for a calibration request from nav\_ctrl\_task, then moves to Calibrating. Calibrating: The car must be stationary. imu\_task collects the reference readings needed by the team’s hump-detection and height-estimation method. On success it reports calibration-done to nav\_ctrl\_task and moves to Ready. On failure it reports an IMU fault and moves to Fault. A mission cannot begin unless calibration succeeds (FR-02). This state is entered from Awaiting Calibration or from Fault. Ready: Calibration has succeeded. imu\_task waits for the mission-start event (the mission state changes to Running). On mission start it resets the highest-hump estimate and moves to Monitoring, unless the mission is resuming from Paused, in which case it keeps the stored estimate. The subsystem also returns here when a mission is paused or ends.  Monitoring: During a mission, imu\_task reads the IMU every 10 ms and classifies the motion event. Tilt and turn rate are reported with the 1 s status message. It checks for hump onset, abnormal motion and read failure. Hump onset moves it to Measuring Hump, an IMU fault moves it to Fault, and a pause or mission end moves it to Ready. It maintains the highest peak estimate for the current mission.  Measuring Hump: Entered on hump onset, with Climbing and Descending phases (matching the climbing-hump and descending-hump events). imu\_task estimates pitch and combines it with the distance travelled between samples to build the height profile. When the hump ends, it records the peak height, updates the mission maximum if it is higher, sends the result for telemetry and returns to Monitoring. If the mission is paused or ends first, or an IMU fault occurs, the unfinished measurement is discarded. A hump is not mistaken for abnormal motion because `[T]`° is set above the steepest hump on the course.  Fault: Entered on any IMU fault (see Terms). imu\_task reports the fault to nav\_ctrl\_task, which places the system in Fault. If the fault is abnormal motion or a read failure during a mission, imu\_task also sets the urgent-stop request (STOP\_IMU) directly to motion\_task, which issues the motor-stop command. imu\_task leaves Fault only when nav\_ctrl\_task, after the fault is reset, sends a new calibration request (Fault → Calibrating). STOP\_IMU stays set until calibration succeeds and nav\_ctrl\_task sends the fault-clear command to motion\_task. Assumption for this statechart: imu\_task estimates pitch θ with a complementary filter on accelerometer and gyro data. Each hump’s height is the sum of Δs × sin θ over the climbing phase, where Δs is the change in distance\_state dist\_mm between consecutive samples (from motion\_task’s encoders; a negative change from reversing is ignored). The peak is the highest value reached. This avoids double-integrating acceleration, which drifts. If the estimate consistently under- or over-reads, a correction factor measured from the reference humps is applied. If distance from motion\_task is unavailable, an estimate from commanded speed and time may be used instead. The thresholds \[T\] and \[A\] and the proposed values N and Y are validated against humps of measured height under assumption A4. Until then, this statechart describes proposed behaviour, not proven accuracy.   |
| :---- |

## **6.5 Subsystem Statechart 5**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name |  Obstacle scanning and avoidance (scan\_task) |
| Related RTOS task(s) | scan\_task owns the HC-SR04 (TRIG GP4, ECHO GP5 via ECHO\_ISR) and the SG90 servo (GP12, PWM slice 6 ch A, 50 Hz). It reads the mission state from nav\_ctrl\_task and the line-found / line-lost result from motion\_task. It sets the urgent-stop flag (STOP\_SCAN) and sends avoidance commands to motion\_task, which is the only task that drives the motors. comms\_task prepares the obstacle-profile and sensor-fault records, and cyw43\_utk\_task publishes them through MQTT. |
| Purpose | Detect an obstacle on the path, stop the car in time, measure the obstacle with a coarse then a fine servo scan, choose stop, continue, turn (bypass) or reverse, and hand back to line following once motion\_task has found the line again (FR-13 to FR-20). |
| Reason a statechart is needed | What scan\_task does with a reading depends on what it is already doing: the same short distance means "stop" while monitoring, "edge found" during a fine scan and "re-plan" during a bypass. Several events are asynchronous (echo arrival, mission pause, line found from motion\_task). The statechart makes the stop and recovery paths explicit, including the case where the sensor stops answering, so the car never drives on blind. |

# 

![][image9]        
Link: [statechart5\_scan\_task.drawio.png](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yynjwgE8vWcfcQiPb3Ez94MNcqUb51fg/view?usp=sharing)  
Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| Terms: \[D\_stop\] is the stopping distance from NFR-08. \[D\_obs\] is the distance within which a scan reading counts as part of the obstacle. \[C\_pass\] is the clearance needed to pass: half the car's width plus a safety margin. \[D\_rev\] is the distance below which the car is too close to turn. All four are set from test data (A5). \[t\_block\] is how long the car may stay stopped in Blocked or Sensor Lost before the mission pauses (10 s, proposed).  Idle: The mission is not Running (Ready, Paused, Finished or Fault). The servo is centred, STOP\_SCAN is clear and the "reverse tried" flag is reset. When the mission state changes to Running, scan\_task moves to Monitoring. Every state returns here whenever the mission is not Running, Fault included, so a stale STOP\_SCAN never blocks recovery. Monitoring: The servo points straight ahead and the sensor pings once per scan period (about 60 ms, one HC-SR04 cycle). Two readings in a row below \[D\_stop\] set STOP\_SCAN, which wakes motion\_task at once (NFR-18), and the task moves to Coarse Scan. Two readings are required so that one false echo does not stop the car. Coarse Scan: With the car stopped, the servo visits five angles from −60° to \+60° in 30° steps. If no angle sees anything within \[D\_obs\], it is a false alarm: STOP\_SCAN is cleared and the task returns to Monitoring (the continue action in FR-17). Right after a reverse, the rescan uses \[D\_obs\] plus the reverse distance, so an obstacle the car has just backed away from is not mistaken for a false alarm. Otherwise it moves to Fine Scan (FR-14). Fine Scan: The servo steps in 5° increments around each edge the coarse scan found, taking a median of three pings at the edge angles. Each reading at distance d and angle θ is converted to a point x \= d·sin θ, y \= d·cos θ. The width is W \= x\_R − x\_L, the closest point is d\_c, and the free space beyond each edge gives the left and right clearance (FR-15, FR-16). The profile goes to the telemetry queue. Planning: scan\_task chooses one action (FR-17). Before sending any command it clears REVERSE\_DONE, LINE\_FOUND and LINE\_LOST on its event flag, so an old reply cannot end this avoidance early. If the side with more clearance has at least \[C\_pass\], it places a bypass command (side and lateral offset) in avoid\_cmd\_mbf, sets CMD, then clears STOP\_SCAN, in that order, and moves to Avoiding. If d\_c is below \[D\_rev\] and no reverse has been tried, it sends a reverse command with STOP\_SCAN still set, waits for REVERSE\_DONE from motion\_task, then rescans. If neither side is passable, or a reverse has already been tried, it moves to Blocked. Avoiding: motion\_task drives the bypass and searches for the line (FR-18, FR-19). scan\_task keeps pinging; a new reading below \[D\_stop\] sets STOP\_SCAN again and sends it back to Coarse Scan to re-plan. LINE\_FOUND from motion\_task returns it to Monitoring (FR-20). LINE\_LOST returns it to Idle, and nav\_ctrl\_task decides what the mission does next. “Reverse tried" is kept until LINE\_FOUND, so a re-plan during the same avoidance cannot reverse again. Blocked: STOP\_SCAN stays set and the car stays stopped (FR-18). scan\_task keeps pinging forward. If the path reads clear for three readings in a row (the obstacle was removed), it clears STOP\_SCAN and returns to Monitoring. If the path is still blocked after \[t\_block\] s, scan\_task sets BLOCKED on nav\_flg and nav\_ctrl\_task moves the mission to Paused. Sensor Lost (fault): Three pings in a row with no echo pulse at all mean the sensor is disconnected or dead. This is different from an out-of-range echo, which is a valid far reading. scan\_task sets STOP\_SCAN, because a car that cannot see ahead must not drive, and sends a sensor-fault record to the telemetry queue. This can happen in Monitoring, Coarse Scan, Fine Scan or Avoiding. Three valid echoes in a row return it to Coarse Scan, not Monitoring, because the path ahead is unknown. If the sensor is still lost after \[t\_block\] s, scan\_task sets BLOCKED on nav\_flg and nav\_ctrl\_task moves the mission to Paused.  Assumption for this statechart: The HC-SR04 running on 3.3 V from Grove 3 gives stable readings over the distances needed (A5), and the beam’s spread can be corrected for when estimating width (to be tested against NFR-20). Until those are tested, the angles, step sizes and thresholds are proposed values.  |

| While Reversing the motors are driving, but STOP\_IMU was only checked once per tick, and the worst-case stop time left out the rest of motion\_task’s current tick. | Fixed | Reversing also waits on STOP\_IMU, and the worst case now includes the rest of the current tick. | Statechart 6.2 (Stopped, Worst-case stop time); NFR-18. |
| Nothing brakes the motors if motion\_task overruns, blocks or stops running, because the PWM keeps its last duty. | Deferred | A hardware watchdog that brakes the motors is a system-level choice and has been raised with the team. motion\_task’s tick overruns will be logged in the NFR-11 test. | NFR-11; raised with the team. |
| motion\_task clears STOP\_IMU on FAULT\_CLEAR(IMU) without checking that imu\_task has recovered. | Rejected with reason | No change. | nav\_ctrl\_task sends FAULT\_CLEAR(IMU) only after imu\_task recalibrates (Section 4; Section 5, Assumption 3), through a buffer with one sender, so it cannot arrive early or out of order. |
| Nothing tells scan\_task or motion\_task that the car is on a hump. A pitched-up car can read the ramp as an obstacle or lose the line and start a line search. | Needs validation | imu\_task shares a hump flag (climbing or descending) with scan\_task and motion\_task. scan\_task then needs more close readings before stopping, and motion\_task allows a longer line-lost time while the flag is set. Details are to be agreed with Buddies 2 and 5\. | Section 4 shared data; 6.2 \[t\_lost\]; 6.5 Monitoring; A4 |
| NFR-05 has no accuracy value (\[X\] cm), so hump-height accuracy can’t pass or fail. | Needs validation | \[X\] stays open until the reference-hump tests are done. The team will traverse humps of measured height 5 times each, record the error of every estimate, and set \[X\] from the results (proposed starting point: 0.5 cm or 20% of the reference height, whichever is larger). The final value goes into NFR-05 before the full mission test. | NFR-05; A4 |

# **9\. Design Consistency**

| Check | Student Response |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Which task owns each hardware device?** |  **CYW43439 WiFi chip on the Pico W module (internal SPI on GP23, GP24, GP25 and GP29, not a Grove port):** cyw43\_utk\_task, the only task that touches the radio or the lwIP/MQTT library. comms\_task owns no hardware; it reaches the network only through message buffers to cyw43\_utk\_task. Motor driver (GP8 to GP11, PWM slices 4 and 5\) and both wheel encoders (left GP0/GP1 on Grove 1, right GP2/GP3 on Grove 2): motion\_task. ENC\_ISR only updates the encoder counters; motion\_task is the only task that writes motor PWM. **Line sensors (GP26/GP27, ADC0/ADC1), barcode sensor (GP7) and battery sense (GP28)**: ir\_sense\_task. barcode\_task owns no hardware. **IMU (I2C0, GP16/GP17):** imu\_task.  **Ultrasonic HC-SR04 (TRIG GP4, ECHO GP5 on Grove 3\) and SG90 servo (GP12, servo port S1):** scan\_task. ECHO\_ISR only timestamps the echo and wakes scan\_task. |
| **Which task has the highest priority, and why?** |  **cyw43\_utk\_task (4, core 0):** the highest priority (number 4\) in the system, fixed by the library and pinned to core 0\. Under SMP each core has its own ready queue, so it can only preempt tasks on core 0\. ir\_sense\_task, motion\_task, imu\_task and scan\_task are pinned to core 1, so the radio cannot delay them. Changing the library is a last resort. **ir\_sense\_task (10, core 1):** the highest-priority control task, because it has the shortest period (1 ms) and a missed sample would distort the line error or the barcode widths. **motion\_task (11, core 1):** High, because it runs the 10 ms PID loop and must brake within 20 ms of STOP\_SCAN or STOP\_IMU (NFR-18). It ranks below ir\_sense\_task and above imu\_task. **imu\_task (12, core 1):** High, because a missed 10 ms sample could miss a tilt fault or a hump peak. It ranks below ir\_sense\_task and motion\_task. **scan\_task (13, core 1):** High, because a late stop decision means a collision. It ranks below the 10 ms tasks because each ultrasonic cycle takes about 60 ms, so its deadline is longer. Its stop does not depend on its own priority: setting STOP\_SCAN wakes motion\_task directly. **barcode\_task (14, core 0):** Medium, because widths are buffered and decoding can wait. **nav\_ctrl\_task (15, core 0):** Medium, because it handles only routine state changes. Urgent stops bypass it. **comms\_task (16 proposed, core 0):** the lowest. Telemetry is useful but never safety-critical, and producers never wait on it, because a full telemetry queue drops and counts the record. |
| **Which subsystem statechart corresponds to which RTOS task or subsystem?** |  **Statechart 6.1** → **comms\_task & cyw43\_utk\_task Statechart 6.2 → motion\_task.** **Statechart 6.3 → ir\_sense\_task** (Region A, plus barcode capture) and barcode\_task (decoding). **Statechart 6.4 → imu\_task.  Statechart 6.5 → scan\_task & nav\_ctrl\_task** |
| **How are functional requirements reflected in the task and statechart design?** |  FR-21: BOOT and WAITING FOR WI-FI; CONNECTING is entered only once a link and IP address exist.  FR-22 and FR-26: STREAMING, with an S line every 1 s and an H heartbeat.  FR-23: each task’s records reach comms\_task through tele\_mbfid and are published as S and E lines. FR-24: comms\_task checks each command from cmd\_mbx against the MQTT specification (snap, ping, map) and counts and logs anything else with no state change.  FR-25: RETRY BACKOFF, and the Wi-Fi-lost reset to WAITING FOR WI-FI, without stopping the mission.  NFR-09, NFR-10 and NFR-17 are tested on cyw43\_utk\_task and comms\_task. FR-04: Line Following. FR-08: Turning. FR-09: distance travelled on every tick. FR-17 and FR-18: Reversing and Bypass. FR-19 and FR-20: Line Search and Line Lost. FR-30: Motion Fault. motion\_task is tested under NFR-02, NFR-04, NFR-07, NFR-08, NFR-10, NFR-11 and NFR-18. FR-02: Calibrating. FR-03 and FR-04: Tracking. FR-05: Junction. FR-06 and FR-07: barcode pipeline. NFR-02, NFR-03 and NFR-11 are tested on ir\_sense\_task and barcode\_task. FR-10 to FR-12: Measuring Hump. FR-27 and FR-29: Monitoring. FR-28 and NFR-13: Fault. NFR-05, NFR-11, NFR-18 and NFR-19 are tested on imu\_task.  FR-13: Monitoring. FR-14 and FR-15: Coarse Scan and Fine Scan. FR-16: Fine Scan. FR-17: Planning. FR-18: Avoiding and Blocked. FR-19 and FR-20: LINE\_FOUND / LINE\_LOST from motion\_task. NFR-06, NFR-07, NFR-08, NFR-18 and NFR-20 are tested on scan\_task. |
| **What changes are still expected after the Week 6 review?** | **WiFi and telemetry**: the comms\_task priority (16 proposed) and a Core column in Section 3; the telemetry record layouts and tele\_mbfid size in messages.h (M7); the barcode action codes and default table with Buddy 3; whether any remote mission command reaches nav\_ctrl\_task; A1 on the demo-day network, with a DHCP retry; and, if the A6 tests show heartbeat gaps, splitting comms\_task into two tasks. **Motion**: the bracketed values and the PID gains will be set from tests, and counts per wheel revolution and the wheelbase will be measured (A2).
